author: Verband Deutscher Büchsenmacher und Waffenfachhändler
extent: Selected contents/introduction and complete section pages 36–42, including policy request, modelling qualifications and citations; remaining document not fully read.
scope_gate: Author describes BMI evaluation questionnaire, rather than a particular draft. Register links several legislative projects; those links are not treated as proof that this questionnaire addresses those exact versions.
observations: Page 40 openly identifies its 4.9% legal-weapon parameter as a reference drawn from seized weapons, not a directly measured 2025 case share. Its use as a model assumption is contestable but not silently mislabelled.

The 5% parameter is attributed to the population impact of severe mental illness. Primary publisher source discovery confirms the named paper gives a 5.2% population-attributable fraction, and the authors’ later reply uses an approximately one-in-twenty explanation. Full paper not yet read, so no clinical/factual-error conclusion follows.
The 1000-person example on page 41 is numerically coherent: about 5 true positive results and 10 false positives under the explicitly assumed 99% sensitivity and specificity.
Claims about the desirability, prediction performance and proportionality of universal screening are not adjudicated from these calculations.
result: No issue promoted from this selected pass. Novelty alone does not make an illustrative model a factual error.
